content_html:
QBism — Observer and Reality

QBism (Quantum Bayesianism) interprets quantum mechanics as a normative framework for an agent’s personal expectations about measurement outcomes. The quantum state (wavefunction) represents degrees of belief, not an objective property of a system. A measurement is an action by the agent upon the world, and the outcome is a new experience for that agent. Probability assignments update by Bayesian inference, with the Born rule serving as a consistency constraint among an agent’s beliefs.

Collapse is not a physical jump in the system; it is the agent’s belief update upon experiencing a result. Objective reality is not denied; QBism reframes quantum theory as a user’s manual for personal expectation and action.

Participatory act: Measurements are interventions, not passive readings.
Personal outcomes: Results are facts for that agent; intersubjective science emerges because all agents use the same coherence rules.
No hidden wave: The wavefunction encodes beliefs, not hidden variables or objective waves.

QBism treats the Born rule as a normative constraint connecting an agent’s probability assignments across possible measurements. It is akin to an extension of Dutch-book coherence into the quantum domain, guiding how to lay consistent bets about experiences.

Concept Classical Copenhagen QBism
Quantum state ψ Objective state of system Objective tool for predicting outcomes Agent’s personal beliefs
Measurement Reveals pre-existing property Causes physical collapse Creates a new experience; triggers belief update
Probability Frequency/chance in world Statistical rule of nature Bayesian degree of belief
Observer Detached Outside but special Participant; centre of inference
Reality Independent, monolithic Partly observation-dependent Participatory & relational (intersubjectively constrained)

QBism resonates with:

Language as Measurement: Naming collapses possibilities into meanings; measurement collapses amplitudes into outcomes.
Misnaming Memory: Each recall is a “measurement” that changes what is remembered (reconsolidation), echoing belief updates.
Select → Change → Reconstruct: Attention as selection, belief revision as change, renewed self-model as reconstruction.
